content_of_post_to_comment: I’m making the same mistake on Substack that I’ve made my whole career. Nuance doesn’t sell. People want someone with a Ph.D. to echo their own pro/anti, yes/no views on a topic. Whether the Ph.D. has actually relevant expertise really doesn’t matter. People want to appeal to an authority they think validates their beliefs. “Well actually, it’s complicated and the truth is somewhere in the middle” doesn’t do that.
comment: Maybe the deeper problem is that expertise has become a form of identity signaling. A nuanced answer asks readers to tolerate uncertainty; a definitive one lets them outsource it. That’s a harder habit to unlearn.
